text: So, the kinds of problems we have looked at so far are largely optimization type of tasks.
So, we are looking for shortest paths in a graph or we are trying to identify the minimum
cost spanning tree or we are looking for the longest common subsequence.
So, we are trying to optimize some quantity, the length of the path or the cost of the
tree or the length of a subsequence.
And then this optimization takes place subject to a constraint.
So, when we are looking for paths, the constraints are given by the graph itself.
So, the path must follow the given edges in the graph.
So, as the graph changes, the path that we identify will also change.
Similarly, we are looking for span entries with respect to a given graph.
So, in each graph, we asked to first identify the different spanning trees and look for the smallest
one among them.
Similarly, with two subsequences, the actual letters in the sequence determine what is common
between them.
So, we can look at a more general formulation of such constraint optimization problems in the
framework of what is called linear programming.
So, in linear programming, we are given some variables, some quantities that we want to calculate.
And then there are some linear functions that constraint these quantities.
A linear function, remember of a variable x is something of the form A x plus b.
So, it has no x square x cube term.
It is all linear.
So, we have A x plus b.
So, in general, then if we have multiple variables x y z, then we could have a constraint
of the form A x plus b y plus something is less than equal to some constant.

text: So, in fact, this is how the very famous simplest algorithm works.
So, what it does is it constructs this feasible region,
which is bounded by our constraints.
And then it picks up vertex.
So, we will not discuss it in detail, but you have to generalize this notion of a corner.
In two dimensions, it is quite easy to imagine what a vertex is.
But in we have multiple constraints as we have to call them to optimize more than two dimensions,
then you need to define vertex properly, but intuitively a vertex is a corner of this feasible region.
So, we started any of these vertices evaluating the objective function.
Then we look at the neighboring vertices.
If any adjacent works, any neighbor has a better value, we move to that neighbor.
If none of our neighbors are better than us in terms of the objective,
then we stop and announce that this vertex is the optimum.
So, we will not go into a proof in this lecture that this is if it is actually correct,
but it is not hard to argue this, but there are of course a lot of details which need to be worked out
to implement simplex correctly.
So, one of the problems with simplex is theoretically it can be exponential.
But actually in practice, it turns out to be a very effective algorithm to solve linear programs.
Now, there are theoretically efficient algorithms.
So, there is a polynomial time algorithm for linear programming.
So, there are the so called interior point methods and there is a method to do to
narrow the curve marker which many people may have heard of.
These are more complicated to describe and program.
Simplex is probably easier to program, but what we need to know as far as we are concerned is that
once you set up a set of constraints and an objective function using linear constraints,
you can solve it efficiently.
So, of course we also have to ask when a solution exists.

So, the first point is that the feasible region will always be convex.
Convex means that if you take any two points inside the region and the region,
and you connect them by a line, the entire line stays in the region.
So, for instance if I have a shape which looks like this, then this is not convex because I can pick two points inside
and then connect it by a line and this line at this portion leaves the region.
So, the feasible space will always be convex, but it could be empty.
Supposing we had had an extra constraint in our earlier thing which says that everything must be below this line.
Now, in addition to the orange if I add this blue constraint, then there is no point that satisfies everything.
So, the constraints are unsatisfiable, the feasible region will become empty and there will be no solutions.
The other possibilities that we do not constrain it enough.
